ai.title: SDK: rename allFiles to projectFiles, add API docs
ai.summary: The `allFiles` parameter in `client.run()` is renamed to `projectFiles` for clarity. Comprehensive API reference documentation added to `sdk/README.md` and JSDoc comments updated in `sdk/src/client.ts`. Scope covers SDK documentation and client interface definitions. Existing code using `allFiles` must update to `projectFiles`.

eli5.text: If you're using the Codebuff assistant tool in your own app, you'll now need to rename an option called 'allFiles' to 'projectFiles', otherwise your code will break. The instructions for how to use the tool have also been expanded with clearer, plain-language descriptions of each setting, so it's easier to know what each option does without guessing. These changes are live today; if you've already built something with the old name, it won't work until you update it.

ai.title: SDK run() accepts agentConfigs array
ai.summary: CodebuffClient.run() replaces singular `agentConfig` object with `agentConfigs` array. New `AgentConfig` type exported from SDK index. Update calls to pass array of config objects instead of key-value map.

eli5.text: You can now tell Codebuff about several custom assistants at once instead of just one. The place where you start a run used to take a single assistant setting; it now takes a list of assistant settings, so you can supply multiple assistants in one go. The published helper now also exports the description for those assistant settings, so you can hand in an array of assistant definitions rather than a single one. Existing single-assistant setups will stop working until updated to the list form, since the old single setting is no longer accepted.

ai.title: bump @codebuff/sdk to 0.1.4
ai.summary: Version bump for @codebuff/sdk from 0.1.3 to 0.1.4. Update affects sdk/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The toolkit's version number was bumped from 0.1.3 to 0.1.4. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping, the only change is the version label in the package file, with no functional differences. You would not notice any new behavior; the toolkit works the same as before. This keeps the version numbering in sync ahead of other planned changes.

ai.title: SDK bundles AgentConfig and ToolName types locally
ai.summary: SDK build copies agent-config.d.ts and tools.d.ts from ../common into src/util/types, replacing direct cross-package imports. client.ts and index.ts now resolve AgentConfig from './util/types/agent-config', decoupling the published package from the monorepo common source. New files sdk/src/util/types/agent-config.ts and tools.ts define the full AgentConfig interface, ToolName union, and ToolParamsMap.

eli5.text: If you build custom Codebuff agents, the type information (like what settings each agent needs and what tools are available) now travels inside the SDK package itself instead of being pulled from a shared internal folder. This means your editor will continue to offer autocomplete and error-checking for your agent files when you use the SDK, even if you install it without the full monorepo setup. The change is live in the SDK build pipeline as of today.

ai.title: Make overrideTools optional in CodebuffClientOptions
ai.summary: The `overrideTools` property in `CodebuffClientOptions` is now optional (`overrideTools?`). The internal `CodebuffClient` class resolves this by defaulting `overrideTools` to an empty object (`{}`) if undefined, while maintaining the type as `NonNullable<CodebuffClientOptions['overrideTools']>` to ensure internal consistency.

eli5.text: If you were setting up a Codebuff assistant and didn't want to customize any of its built-in capabilities, you can now leave that setup field blank instead of having to fill in an empty placeholder. The assistant treats a missing value the same as an empty settings list, so nothing changes in how it behaves unless you actively provide custom settings. This is already live today for anyone integrating the SDK, and it just removes a required step when you don't need it.

eli5.text: The package version number for the developer tool kit was quietly increased, marking the latest routine release. If you rely on this kit for building integrations, you'll pick up the new version automatically on your next dependency update; otherwise nothing visibly changes. This is behind-the-scenes version housekeeping with no new features or behavior.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.6 simplifies publish script and moves agent config types
ai.summary: SDK version bumped to 0.1.6. `publish.js` simplified by removing dist-directory path rewriting, now publishing directly from the sdk directory. `agent-config` and `tools` types moved from `src/util/types` to `src/types` via build script, with `package.json` paths updated to `./dist/sdk/src/`.

eli5.text: If you use the Codebuff assistant tool inside your project, the setup file it shares with other tools has been moved to a simpler, more standard location. This means the helper that installs and updates the tool no longer has to shuffle files around into a temporary folder before publishing it, reducing the chance of a failed installation. The change is already live, and you'd only notice it if you were checking where the files live on your computer.

ai.title: Fix expireMessages logic in backend messages util
ai.summary: Corrected filter logic in expireMessages within backend/src/util/messages.ts. Previous implementation incorrectly retained agentStep messages due to hardcoded false condition. Now properly removes messages where timeToLive is agentStep or userPrompt matching endOf agentStep.

eli5.text: Messages that the assistant stores while helping you are now being cleared out at the right time instead of hanging around past when they should be gone. Specifically, step-by-step progress notes the assistant writes during a task, and the prompts you send at the end of a task, are now removed when each task finishes, rather than incorrectly being kept. This only matters if you notice the assistant remembering old step details it should have forgotten. The fix is live today in the backend that powers the assistant.

ai.title: Fix expireMessages userPrompt retention condition
ai.summary: Corrected logic in expireMessages. Changed condition from endOf === 'agentStep' to endOf === 'userPrompt'. Ensures userPrompt messages are retained only when appropriate.

eli5.text: The system now correctly clears out old assistant messages that were tied to a single user question, instead of mistakenly clearing messages tied to each step the assistant takes. This affects internal logging behavior on the backend, so you wouldn't notice it directly, but it ensures message cleanup happens at the right time during conversations.

ai.title: Add spawnagentinline tool for context-preserving agent delegation
ai.summary: New `spawn_agent_inline` tool allows spawning a single agent that executes within the current message history, preserving context and added messages upon return. Implemented in `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts` and registered across `common/src/tools/constants.ts` and `list.ts` files. Unlike `spawn_agents`, this tool has no tool result and ends the agent step, requiring `end_turn` to return control. Also updated `set_messages` params to pass through additional properties.

eli5.text: The assistant can now launch a mini-assistant that works inside the current conversation without losing track of what has been discussed. When you ask it to do something, that mini-assistant sees all the messages so far and any new notes it leaves behind stay in the conversation when it finishes. Unlike other delegation tools, this one does not come back with a summary result; it simply stops, and you have to take back control manually. The change landed on 2025-08-10 and is part of the backend system, so you would notice it if you use the assistant through a developer tool or integration that exposes the new capability.

ai.title: Format generated tool definitions
ai.summary: scripts/generate-tool-definitions.ts now executes npx prettier --write on the output file after writing tools.d.ts. This ensures generated definitions match project formatting standards automatically. Scope limited to the generation script.

eli5.text: When the team regenerates the list of tools the assistant can use, the system now automatically tidies that file's layout before saving it. Previously the freshly generated file could look messy until someone manually cleaned it up later. Any developer who runs the tool-generation step will now see the file appear already formatted. The formatting step runs every time the definitions are regenerated, so the saved file always matches the project's style guide without extra effort. This is an internal developer tool, so end users won't notice anything directly, but it keeps the generated files consistent for anyone working on the project.

ai.title: Tool description comments switch line to JSDoc
ai.summary: compile-tool-definitions.ts jsonSchemaToTypeScript emits /** ... */ instead of // ... for schema property descriptions. tools.d.ts regenerated: AddSubgoalParams, BrowserLogsParams, CodeSearchParams fields now carry JSDoc block comments. Affects shared core types only. IDE hover tooltips pick up property docs where line comments were invisible.

eli5.text: If you hover your mouse over a field in the assistant's tool definitions inside a code editor, you will now see a helpful description pop up where previously nothing appeared. The developers switched from plain line comments (which the editor cannot display) to formatted block comments (which it can), so the explanations you wrote for each field are now visible when someone inspects them. This only affects shared definitions used across the assistant's tools and takes effect immediately.

ai.title: Add spawnagentinline tool renderer
ai.summary: Added `spawn_agent_inline` to `toolRenderers` in `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts`. Implements `onToolStart` header, `onParamEnd` for `agent_type` (resolving display name via `Client.getInstance`) and `prompt`, and `onToolEnd` spinner activation. Scope limited to CLI tool output rendering.

eli5.text: If you run the command-line tool and an agent inline task starts, the terminal now shows a 'Spawn Agent Inline' header followed by the agent type and prompt as they arrive, then a spinner that says 'Agent running inline...' while the agent works. This only changes how that specific kind of task is displayed in your terminal output; nothing about how the task runs behind the scenes changed.

ai.title: Remove setoutput from base agents
ai.summary: Removed `set_output` from `toolNames` in `.agents/base.ts`, `.agents/base-experimental.ts`, `.agents/base-lite.ts`, `.agents/base-max.ts`, and `backend/src/templates/agents/base.ts`. Fixes validation errors in agent configurations. Also updated `.agents/brainstormer.ts` to include `spawn_agents` and changed `.agents/git-committer.ts` output mode to `last_message`.

eli5.text: The assistant has been quietly simplified so it no longer tries to set a value as one of its available actions, which had been causing small configuration errors in five base setup files and one shared template. You won't see this directly, but the assistant will now load its tool list without the validation warnings that were interrupting some setups. Two other companion assistants also got small adjustments: one now has access to a feature for creating sub-assistants, and another will return its response as plain text instead of structured data. These changes are already in place and affect only internal agent configurations.

ai.title: Rename agent json output mode to structured output
ai.summary: The 'json' value of agent outputMode has been renamed to 'structured_output' across schema validation, runtime checks, and template configs. This is a naming normalization for the structured output mode, keeping the set_output tool coupling intact. The type definitions, type declaration files, and example agents are updated together with the knowledge docs and tests.
ai.evidence: Renames the agent output mode literal from 'json' to 'structured_output' across the schema enum and refine checks in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts (e.g. data.outputMode === 'structured_output'), the runtime check in backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts (agentTemplate.outputMode === 'structured_output'), the template outputMode: 'structured_output' in backend/src/templates/agents/agent-builder.ts, base-agent-builder.ts, and file-explorer.ts, the AgentTemplate type in common/src/types/agent-template.ts, the type declaration files common/src/util/types/agent-config.d.ts and sdk/src/types/agent-config.ts, and the example agents common/src/util/example-1.ts, example-2.ts, and example-3.ts, with knowledge doc and test updates.
ai.migration: If you author custom agents using outputMode 'json', rename that literal to 'structured_output' and keep the set_output tool in toolNames; agents that omit outputSchema still default to last_message.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether any dynamic agent JSON templates shipped with users still use the old 'json' literal.

changes.what: Renames the Zod enum variant and refine checks from 'json' to 'structured_output'.
Renames the outputMode union member from 'json' to 'structured_output'.
Updates the runtime outputMode comparison from 'json' to 'structured_output'.
Updates the agent-builder, base-agent-builder, and file-explorer template outputMode values from 'json' to 'structured_output'.
Updates the agent-config type declarations and docs in both common and sdk packages.
Updates the example-1.ts, example-2.ts, example-3.ts outputMode literals and the dynamic-agents.knowledge.md comments.

ai.title: Remove sendagentmessage tool
ai.summary: Removed `send_agent_message` tool definition, handler, and params from backend and common packages. Deleted `sendAgentMessageTool`, `handleSendAgentMessage`, and `sendAgentMessageParams`. Updated `superagent` template to drop the tool from `toolNames` and remove inter-agent messaging prompt instructions. Modified `spawn-agents-async` description to remove references to parent-child communication via messages.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff's assistant that spawns helper assistants to tackle parts of a coding task, those helpers can no longer exchange notes with each other or with their parent assistant using a dedicated messaging tool. The feature that let one assistant send a structured message (prompt plus extra data) to another has been removed entirely, along with the special instructions that told the parent assistant to use it. Async-spawned helpers still run independently, but they now report results through the normal task-completion flow instead of interrupting each other mid-task. The change is live in the 2025-08-10 release for anyone using the async multi-agent workflow.

ai.title: Optional terminal params, toolResult string type
ai.summary: Zod `.optional()` applied to `process_type` and `timeout_seconds` in `run-terminal-command.ts`. `ToolResult` type changed to `string` in `agent-config.d.ts` and `tools.d.ts`. Scope: Shared/Core types and tool params. Detail: handleSteps expects tool results as strings.

eli5.text: You can now tell the terminal helper to run in the background without also having to say how long to wait, and you can leave the default waiting mode out too. Behind the scenes, the assistant now treats every result it gets back from running a tool as a simple piece of text, instead of a mixed bag of different things, which makes the steps it takes next more reliable. In short: fewer things you have to fill in, and steadier behavior once the command starts.
